context_characters.note: Measured after semantic correctness, never before. The V1 duplicate-payload target CONTRAST_MATRIX_ROW_PAYLOAD does not arise here: the V2 path has no contrast matrix, and the classification carries an evaluation tree rather than repeated feature id lists.
context_characters.tokens_not_reported_because: No local tokenizer is installed, and characters are not equated with tokens.

copyright.method: Every artifact is scanned for the longest run of consecutive tokens also occurring in the locally indexed Toronto Notes corpus, seeded on 12-word matches. The fingerprint set is built in memory and never written.

decision.basis: The counterfactual gate passed on all six precommitted limbs. Accepted-item safety is perfect: 4 accepted items score zero on all eleven dimensions. Over the same ten opportunities acceptance moved from 2 to 4 and the reviewers' defect count over all realized items moved from 45 to 1. All four diagnosed defect classes are zero in the realized V2 items, and fail-closed is now common and correctly placed: five opportunities never reach prose, each refused by the defect the diagnosis named.
decision.medium_36_pilot_reason: The whole frozen opportunity universe is 30, which is fewer than the 36 the specified pilot needs. Only 18 of those 30 carry the demanded response class and decision granularity the pre-stem predicates require, because the option set contract was authored for the contrast-first sample and for no other opportunity. Sixteen of the 18 reach three admissible curated candidates, and ten of those are consumed by this replay, leaving six. Building 36 would require authoring new opportunities, new competitive contrast seed packs with independent seed review, and new current-source evidence packets, which is the source-packet research stage rather than an architecture pilot, and the repository policy forbids inventing seeds or reconstructing evidence.
decision.next_bottleneck_detail: Not retrieval, which the four-arm benchmark settled, and no longer the relation model. It is that the curated competitive contrast library carries three usable competitors for too few opportunities once V2's coherence rules remove the nested, redundant and anchor-equals-condition members, and that 12 of the 30 frozen opportunities have no authored option-set contract at all. Runner-up: the model has no gate for an out-of-set concept that shares every discriminator with the key, which is what rejected G2-OBGYN-01.
decision.scaling_rationale: Sixty-eight relations were enough to settle ten opportunities, and they were built from material the repository already holds. Precomputing all concept pairs over a 1,595-page corpus is the combinatorial explosion the design refuses, and the benchmark already showed retrieval is not the constraint. Populate on demand: opportunity, bounded retrieval against the existing chunk index, candidate concepts, pairwise relations, evidence validation, persistent cache. Keep the concept, evidence and contrast graphs separate.
decision.the_finding_that_matters_most: The binding constraint has moved. Under V1 it was the contrast-relation model, and seven of eight rejections traced to it. Under V2 it is contrast supply: four of the five refusals are a set falling below three competitors, and the medium pilot cannot be built because only 18 of the 30 frozen opportunities carry an authored option-set contract at all. The architecture is no longer what limits safe items; the curated library is.
decision.what_it_demonstrably_did_not_do: It did not raise yield. Five of ten opportunities produce nothing, four of those because the curated contrast library has fewer than three usable competitors once the unusable ones are dropped. V2 converts unsafe items into no items, which is the right trade and is not the same as producing more.
decision.what_the_architecture_demonstrably_did: It moved failure upstream. V1 realized ten items and an independent reviewer rejected eight of them; V2 realizes five, four are accepted, and the five it refuses are refused before a stem exists, by the specific defect each one carries. Silence-as-absence defects fell from 15 to 0, ten disjunctive conditions are now read as disjunctions, and the two accepted V1 controls survive unchanged.
decision.why_this_is_not_VALIDATED: Two limbs are missing. The specified medium pilot cannot be run at all, so the architecture has never been exercised outside the ten opportunities its relation readings were authored for, and four accepted items across two disciplines cannot distinguish an architecture that works from one that works on population-health and cardiology material. And the model still has no rule for the defect that rejected its one rejected item: a concept outside the option set that shares every available discriminator with the key. That was caught by a human reading, not by a gate.

difficulty.note: Structural difficulty judged by the reviewer against the declared intent. This is not empirical difficulty: no candidate has answered any of these items.

protocol.standard: Section 14.2 of the design, precommitted before any V2 item existed: any count above zero on the eleven safety dimensions rejects the item.

results.lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in his management?

options.label: A
options.rationale: Hypotension with a raised jugular venous pressure and clear lung fields in an inferior ST-elevation infarct identifies right-ventricular infarction physiology, in which cardiac output depends on right-sided filling. CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 directs cautious preload optimization with intravenous fluid and reassessment of fluid responsiveness for the hypotension, alongside the reperfusion that is already being arranged.
options.text: Give a cautious intravenous fluid bolus and reassess fluid responsiveness

options.label: B
options.rationale: Plausible: reducing myocardial oxygen demand is a standard early move in an ST-elevation infarct, and his heart rate and pain invite it. Inferior: the stem states hypotension, and CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 says not to initiate or escalate beta blockade during a low-output state or with cardiogenic-shock risk, and to reassess after stabilization. The condition under which this becomes right, a patient out of the low-output state, is the opposite of what the stem describes.
options.text: Give intravenous metoprolol to reduce myocardial oxygen demand

options.label: C
options.rationale: Plausible: a jugular venous pressure visible at the earlobe reads as volume overload, and a loop diuretic is the reflex response to it. Inferior: the stem states that the lung fields are clear, so there is no pulmonary congestion for a diuretic to relieve, and the raised filling pressure here is the physiology sustaining output rather than a surplus. The same claim directs avoiding preload-reducing diuretics in this pattern.
options.text: Give intravenous furosemide for the raised jugular venous pressure

options.label: D
options.rationale: Plausible: the blood pressure is 78/50 mmHg and vasoactive support is part of managing infarct-related shock. Inferior: preload has not yet been optimized, and CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 puts a cautious fluid challenge with reassessment first in exactly this pattern. CLM-ACS-AMI-CARDIOGENIC-SHOCK-01 reserves vasoactive support for persistent hypotension or a vasopressor requirement with end-organ hypoperfusion, which is the point at which this option becomes the right one.
options.text: Start a norepinephrine infusion

results.stem: A 64-year-old man arrives at a community emergency department 70 minutes after the sudden onset of heavy central chest pain. His electrocardiogram shows 3 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal depression in I and aVL. The regional percutaneous coronary intervention centre has accepted him and the transfer arranged will place him on the catheterisation laboratory table well inside the accepted first-medical-contact-to-device interval. While the transfer is being organised his blood pressure falls to 78/50 mmHg. His jugular venous pressure is visible at the earlobe with the head of the bed at 45 degrees, and his lung fields are clear throughout.

stem_blueprint_v2.key_concept: Give a cautious intravenous fluid bolus and reassess fluid responsiveness

required_features.normalized_feature: device therapy is reachable inside the accepted interval
the electrocardiogram is diagnostic of ST-elevation myocardial infarction
hypotension with an elevated jugular venous pressure and clear lung fields is present

results.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-R2-OB-MASTITIS-ANCHOR describes an increasingly erythematous, oedematous and painful region of the breast with systemic signs such as fever and chills, and CLM-GEN-OB-DX-01 adds unilateral localized tenderness, erythema and heat with fever or malaise. One segment of one breast is involved on day eleven with a fever of 38.6 degrees, which is that pattern.
options.text: Bacterial mastitis

options.label: B
options.rationale: Plausible: an abscess is a progression of this same infection and shares its systemic features, so nothing in the fever or the erythema separates the two. Inferior: CLM-R2-OB-ABSCESS describes progressive induration and erythema with often a palpable fluid collection in a well-defined area, and CLM-GEN-OB-INV-01 makes fluctuance the finding that raises the concern. The stem states that no fluctuant area and no pocket of fluid can be felt, which is the condition under which this would be the answer.
options.text: Lactational breast abscess

options.label: C
options.rationale: Plausible: the swelling decreases temporarily after a feed, which is exactly the behaviour CLM-R4-OB-GALACTOCELE describes for a galactocele. Inferior: the same claim says a galactocele does not carry erythema or systemic symptoms unless it becomes infected, and the stem states both a red, warm segment and a fever with rigors.
options.text: Galactocele

options.label: D
options.rationale: Plausible: a red, swollen breast in a young woman is the presentation that must not be assumed benign, and CLM-R2-OB-IBC makes any concern for it an urgent referral. Inferior: that claim raises the concern on skin thickening, breast retraction and a peau d'orange appearance, none of which is described here, while the acute fever and rigors of the last day belong to the infective picture rather than to a neoplastic one.
options.text: Inflammatory breast cancer

results.stem: A 29-year-old woman is seen on the eleventh day after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. She is breastfeeding and describes two days of increasing pain in the upper outer part of her right breast. That segment is red, swollen, warm and tender, and the swelling becomes noticeably smaller for a while after her baby has fed from that side. Her temperature is 38.6 degrees Celsius and she has felt shivery and generally unwell since yesterday. No fluctuant area and no pocket of fluid can be felt anywhere in the breast.

required_features.normalized_feature: a palpable fluctuant fluid collection is present
the mass decreases temporarily after a feed
fever or other systemic symptoms are present
one breast segment is erythematous, oedematous and painful

blind_solver.difficulty_comment: Four results have to be read together, but each competitor is closed by its own stated result, so the reasoning is checklist-like once the pattern is seen.
blind_solver.reasoning: Survival measured from diagnosis is longer while deaths are unchanged, which is what happens when the diagnosis date moves earlier and the date of death does not. The three usual competitors are each closed by a stated result: randomisation removes self-selection, an equal cumulative number diagnosed removes an excess of detected disease, and an equal grade distribution removes an excess of slowly progressing tumours.

results.lead_in: Which explanation best accounts for this pattern of results?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-R2-PHELO-LEAD-TIME describes the delay between the point at which disease becomes detectable by screening and the point at which it would have been diagnosed from symptoms, and warns that judging a programme by survival time after diagnosis gives a falsely positive impression. Every element of that is here: the diagnosis date moves earlier, the survival clock therefore starts earlier, and the date of death does not move, which is why mortality is unchanged while measured survival is four years longer.
options.text: Lead-time bias

options.label: B
options.rationale: Plausible: better outcomes in a screened group are very often explained by who chooses to be screened, and CLM-R2-PHELO-HEALTHY-VOLUNTEER says such comparisons tend to favour the screened. Inferior: that mechanism needs groups that selected themselves, and the stem states that participants were randomly assigned and comparable at entry, which is the condition under which this explanation would apply.
options.text: Healthy screenee (selection) bias

options.label: C
options.rationale: Plausible: intermittent screening does preferentially catch slowly progressing disease, and CLM-R2-PHELO-LENGTH explains why that inflates survival. Inferior: that mechanism requires an excess of slow-progressing variants among screen-detected cases, and the stem states that the distribution of tumour grade was the same in both groups.
options.text: Length-time bias

options.label: D
options.rationale: Plausible: overdiagnosis also produces longer measured survival with unchanged mortality, so the two headline results alone do not separate it from the answer. Inferior: CLM-R2-PHELO-OVERDIAGNOSIS identifies it by an excess of cancers diagnosed in the screened group, and the stem states that the cumulative number diagnosed was the same in the two groups.
options.text: Overdiagnosis

results.stem: A national trial randomly assigned 80,000 adults either to a new screening test for a solid tumour or to usual care, and the two groups were comparable at entry. After twelve years of follow-up the cumulative number of cancers diagnosed was the same in the two groups, and the distribution of tumour grade among the cancers found was also the same in the two groups. Deaths from the cancer did not differ between the groups. Among people whose cancer was found by screening, however, the average time from diagnosis to death was four years longer than among those diagnosed in usual care.

required_features.normalized_feature: cumulative incidence is the same in both groups
slowly progressing variants are over-represented among screen-detected cases
disease-specific mortality is unchanged between the groups
participants were randomised and the groups are comparable at baseline
measured survival from diagnosis is longer in the screened group

results.lead_in: Which revision to the letter would best protect the autonomy of the people invited?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-R4-PHELO-ABSOLUTE contrasts a relative statement, which sounds impressive, with an absolute figure, which is what actually helps an individual decide, and CLM-R4-PHELO-FALSEPOS supplies the corresponding harm that a first-time attender faces. CLM-R2-PHELO-ACCEPTABILITY says autonomy may be compromised by the way information is given, so where informed choice is the stated objective the figures given have to be ones the reader can apply to themselves.
options.text: Give the absolute chance of benefit and of a false positive result

options.label: B
options.rationale: Plausible: a voluntariness statement is itself an autonomy measure, and CLM-R2-PHELO-REMINDERS warns that people who read more authority into an invitation than it has may abdicate their right to informed consent. Inferior: that is the repair for a letter whose defect is that readers feel obliged to attend, and the defect the stem describes is a different one, that the only benefit figure given cannot be applied to the reader.
options.text: Add a statement that participation is voluntary and that declining will not affect any other care

options.label: C
options.rationale: Plausible: it replaces a relative figure with a real count, which looks like the concrete information the letter is missing. Inferior: a detection count without the number invited and without the harms is another figure the reader cannot apply to themselves, and the stem states that the letter carries no denominator and no account of harm. Its condition, that the reader already has both, is not met.
options.text: Add the number of cancers the programme detected last year

options.label: D
options.rationale: Plausible: sensitivity and specificity are the standard description of a screening test's performance and belong in programme documentation, per CLM-R4-PHELO-ACTION-POLICY. Inferior: they describe the test rather than the reader's own chance of benefit or harm, and CLM-R2-PHELO-ACCEPTABILITY makes protecting autonomy a matter of how the information lands with the person invited, which is the objective the stem states.
options.text: Add the sensitivity and specificity of the screening test

results.stem: A regional screening programme is rewriting the letter it sends to the people it invites for a first screening test. The programme board has agreed that the purpose of the rewrite is to protect the autonomy of those invited, so that each of them can make their own decision about whether to attend. The current letter describes the benefit in one sentence: that screening reduces deaths from the disease by about a third. It says nothing else about how much benefit an individual can expect.

stem_blueprint_v2.key_concept: Replace the relative benefit figure with the absolute chance of benefit and the chance of a false positive result

required_features.normalized_feature: the stated objective of the revision is to protect the autonomy of those invited
the invitation states a relative benefit figure and nothing else about benefit

competitor_verdicts.concept: Launch as planned with continuing evaluation against programme goals
Launch in a single district as a pilot and expand later
Raise the threshold so that fewer results are called positive

results.lead_in: What should the programme do about the planned launch?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-GEN-PHELO-ORG-01 makes coordinated capacity for confirmatory diagnosis and treatment a requirement of a screening programme and says a test should not be launched at population scale when that pathway cannot be delivered. CLM-R4-PHELO-HARM-LABEL names the harm precisely: labelling asymptomatic people as possibly having a disease when the investigation cannot follow, or diagnosing them with no treatment to offer. CLM-R2-PHELO-FACILITIES reaches the same conclusion where follow-up is not accessible.
options.text: Defer the launch until diagnostic and treatment capacity is in place

options.label: B
options.rationale: Plausible: continuing evaluation against defined goals is a genuine requirement, CLM-R4-PHELO-EVALUATION states it, and this programme already has the goals and the plan the stem describes. Inferior: it is a requirement of a programme that does launch, and the stem states the confirmatory pathway cannot take the expected numbers. Evaluating a programme as it produces positives it cannot investigate does not prevent that harm.
options.text: Launch as planned with continuing evaluation against programme goals

options.label: C
options.rationale: Plausible: reducing scale is the usual way to launch within a constraint, and CLM-R2-PHELO-COST-CONTINUITY notes that population-scale cost is what makes screening hard to sustain. Inferior: a pilot works where the constraint is cost or logistics, and the stem describes an absolute shortfall in the confirmatory pathway with no additional capacity available at all, so a single district reproduces the same failure on a smaller scale.
options.text: Launch in a single district as a pilot and expand later

options.label: D
options.rationale: Plausible: raising the threshold does reduce the number of positive results and therefore the referral load, and CLM-R2-PHELO-CUTOFF treats the placement of the cut-off as a real design decision. Inferior: that claim makes a cut-off set too far toward the low-risk end a matter of investigating and reassuring large numbers of low-risk people, and the stem does not describe that. Moving the threshold does not create a confirmatory pathway, and the people who still screen positive meet the same shortfall.
options.text: Raise the threshold so that fewer results are called positive

results.stem: A provincial health authority has finished planning a population screening programme for a chronic condition. The programme has written goals, a defined target population and an evaluation plan that will report against those goals each year. During final preparations the authority establishes that the specialist clinics that would confirm the diagnosis in people who screen positive, and the services that would treat them, cannot take the numbers the programme expects, and that no additional confirmatory or treatment capacity can be secured for the foreseeable future.

stem_blueprint_v2.key_concept: Defer the launch until diagnostic and treatment capacity is in place

required_features.normalized_feature: diagnostic and treatment capacity for those who screen positive is not in place
the programme has defined goals and an evaluation plan

G2-MED-03.comment: The three findings are a natural sequence for a community department stabilising a transfer, and nothing in the stem exists only to kill an option: the low pressure, the raised venous pressure and the clear lungs are one physiological pattern, not three separate insertions. Both reflex answers, beta blockade for demand and a diuretic for the venous pressure, are defeated by findings the stem states rather than by findings it withholds, which is what makes the item hard honestly. The vasopressor option is settled differently and correctly: the stem does not claim end-organ hypoperfusion is absent, and the rationale does not either. It says preload has not yet been optimized and names the point at which the option becomes right.
observations: CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 names right-precordial ST elevation, especially V4R, as supporting the pattern. The stem does not give a right-sided tracing. The claim's grammar makes the clinical triad the identifying finding and V4R supportive, so the key rationale is within the claim, but an item at this level would be stronger with V4R stated.
A right-sided electrocardiogram is a reasonable parallel action a candidate might want. It is an investigation rather than a management step and does not displace the haemodynamic answer.

G2-OBGYN-01.REJECT_REASON: The keyed answer is not uniquely supported against a concept the item's own evidence defines. CLM-R2-OB-MASTITIS-ANCHOR describes inflammatory mastitis as an increasingly erythematous, oedematous and painful region of the breast with systemic signs and symptoms such as fever and chills, which is the stem word for word, and separates bacterial mastitis from it only as the progression that needs antibiotics to resolve. That is a response-to-treatment criterion; nothing available at presentation settles it. A candidate reasoning from the item's own cited packet could answer inflammatory mastitis and be right. Inflammatory mastitis is not among the options, so this is a best answer the option set cannot contain.
G2-OBGYN-01.comment: The three distractors are well handled and each is defeated on a stated finding or a cited discriminator: no fluctuance for the abscess, fever and erythema against the galactocele, and the absence of skin thickening and peau d'orange against the carcinoma. The stem is natural and the single explicit denial reads as an ordinary examination sentence. The defect is upstream of all of that. It is in the key concept's granularity: 'bacterial mastitis' sits one level finer than any feature in the frozen vocabulary can resolve.
observations: This is the same underlying problem the V1 item hit from the other side. There the key rationale had to render a cited claim as its categorical inverse to explain a firm non-fluctuant mass away; here the mass is not stated and the unresolvable neighbour is inflammatory mastitis instead of phlegmon. Both are the mastitis spectrum being finer than the option set.

G2-PHELO-01.comment: Every element of the results paragraph is something a trial report would carry, and each competing explanation is closed by one of them rather than by a sentence written to close it. Randomisation with comparable groups closes self-selection, an equal cumulative number diagnosed closes overdiagnosis, and an equal grade distribution closes length-time. The three distractors are the three explanations a candidate actually reaches for, and none is defeated by anything the stem leaves unsaid. The rationales name the specific stated result that settles each one.
observations: Tumour grade is a proxy for growth rate rather than growth rate itself, so the length-time exclusion rests on the standard operationalisation of that bias rather than on a direct measurement. This is how the bias is assessed in practice and the rationale does not claim more.

The option-realization contract flags OPTION_SPECIFICITY_MISMATCH because 'Overdiagnosis' is one word beside 'Healthy screenee (selection) bias'. The key is itself among the shortest options, so the length spread does not point at it and no cue is created.

G2-PHELO-02.comment: The stem states two things and both do work: the objective the board has set, and what the letter currently says about benefit. The three distractors are the three revisions a programme would actually consider, and each is defeated on content the stem gives. The detection-count rationale is the one to check, because it could easily have said the reader lacks the denominator when the stem is silent; it does not, it says the letter carries no denominator and no account of harm, which the stem states outright.
observations: Declared residual risk from the blind solve: the stem does not say whether the letter already tells people that attending is a choice, so a candidate could read the autonomy objective as calling first for a voluntariness statement. The stem describes one concrete deficiency and asks which revision best serves the objective, and the described deficiency is what the answer repairs, so the best answer is determinate. It would be more secure if the letter's existing voluntariness wording were stated.

G2-PHELO-03.comment: Safe and clean. The shortfall is the operative fact, the programme's planning strengths are stated so that the launch-with-evaluation option is genuinely attractive, and the pilot and threshold options are defeated by what the shortfall is rather than by silence about them. The threshold option is the one the stem does not directly address, and the rationale settles it on the discriminator rather than by claiming the threshold is correctly placed.
observations: Declared HARD, reads EASY. The shortfall is stated as absolute and unfixable, which is what makes the item safe and is also what leaves little to infer. This is the same tension the difficulty analysis of the V1 pilot recorded on this opportunity, and it is not repaired here.
